text.p: A court in Cameroon has jailed two journalists from the newspaper Le Messager for insulting President Paul Biya and members of the national assembly, their lawyer said on Friday.

The appeals court in the commercial capital Douala jailed publisher Pius Njawe for six months and journalist Eyoum Ngangue for 12 months on Thursday, after they appealed against an earlier ruling imposing a 2.5 million CFA franc ($4,835) fine.
Their lawyer, Chretien Boumo, told Reuters that they would appeal.
The case dates back to an article published in December 1995.
"Neither the president nor the assembly members sued. It was the public prosecutor who sued," Boumo said. "Curiously the (appeal) judge sentenced my clients to custodial sentences. We will appeal."
Le Messager is no stranger to such cases. Since March it has been locked in a case involving the minister of territorial administration who has accused it of spread false information.
